- If sentiment shows strong bullish (≥0.33) or bearish (≤-1.0) momentum in recent days, model should adjust forecast downward or upward respectively, especially if price has recently spiked or dipped sharply.
- Model tends to overestimate price increases after a spike (e.g., 2023-12-21, 2024-05-15–17) — apply downward correction for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (mostly 0.00–0.25), model often underestimates volatility — increase forecast range or add 2–3% buffer for mean reversion.
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal from high (e.g., 2024-05-16–17) or low (e.g., 2023-12-21), model often fails to anticipate direction — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 2–3 days prior.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates downside risk in bearish sentiment periods — add 5–10% downward bias if sentiment ≤ -0.5 over last 5 days.
- Model overfits to recent trend — if last 5 prices are rising, forecast should not exceed 1.5x recent high unless sentiment confirms breakout.
